headline: High: Dify can write and execute server-side code while TREK exposes collaborative MCP/browser surfaces, creating dangerous cross-agent injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can write files, execute shell, and wire tools into agent/workflow apps; TREK uses MCP and browser-based collaborative flows. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if TREK content is fed into Dify or vice versa, though the exact bridge is undocumented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF TREK content is passed into a Dify agent prompt or tool input without sanitization
IF Dify workflows render TREK-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of TREK outputs into Dify prompts
Add a fixed instruction/content separator in any shared workflow
Require manual review before Dify executes TREK-derived tool calls
Use allowlisted templates for any cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs, knowledge base content, and model-provider/tool credentials; TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets. Dify also has broad network egress, while TREK has allowlisted egress and shared collaborative state. If either side forwards shared data into the other’s outputs or external APIs, sensitive travel and secret material can leak.
conditions: IF TREK secrets or reservations are copied into Dify conversation logs or knowledge files
IF Dify tool outputs containing TREK data are sent to third-party model providers
mitigations: Keep TREK secrets out of Dify prompts and uploads
Redact API keys, MFA secrets, and confirmation numbers before transfer
Restrict Dify model-provider egress for shared workflows
Separate operator accounts and credentials between the two systems
Review logs for accidental cross-system data copies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and server-side code execution; TREK has collaborative real-time state, MCP, and writable local files like ./data/travel.db and ./uploads/. Both can mutate shared resources, so concurrent writes or tool actions can conflict. The exact shared directory is not specified, so I avoid high severity and escalate only to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem or database
IF Dify server-side code and TREK collaborative edits run concurrently on shared state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories and databases
Serialize writes with a simple lock file or queue
Disable concurrent edits during shared operations
Snapshot shared files before running cross-agent tasks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate agent/workflow outputs and TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK treats Dify output as authoritative, a bad plan or hallucinated fact can cascade into downstream travel actions. There is no direct evidence of automatic execution, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF TREK consumes Dify-generated text without verification
IF Dify-produced itinerary facts are used to update reservations or plans
mitigations: Require human verification before TREK acts on Dify output
Add source citations to Dify-generated recommendations
Compare Dify output against external travel sources before use
Flag low-confidence items for manual review

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, documents, photos, country visit history, user accounts, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets. Dify handles conversation logs, knowledge base content, and model-provider/tool credentials. If TREK personal data is routed into Dify, residency, retention, and secret-handling obligations can be breached; Dify’s docs-only profile does not show matching compliance controls.
conditions: IF EU personal data from TREK is stored in Dify logs or knowledge files
IF TREK secrets are processed by Dify without a DPA or retention controls
mitigations: Keep regulated travel data out of Dify unless policy is confirmed
Set explicit retention limits on Dify logs
Mask email addresses, confirmation numbers, and secrets before transfer
Document data-flow ownership for both systems
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the integration
